title: fix(objectql): withhold caller-supplied readonly values from beforeInsert (#22306)
body:
Fixes #22306
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What was wrong

On a non-system create, `ObjectQL.insert` dispatched `beforeInsert` on the caller's payload. It ran the static `readonly` strip (`staticReadonlyCreateStrip`) only after the hooks. Take a hook that stamps a read-only column only when the column is absent, the hotcrm `if (!input.stage_entry_date)` shape. It saw the caller's value and did nothing, then the strip dropped that value, so the row stored NULL where the hook would have stamped today. The update path has withheld these values from its hooks since #16344. The insert path did not.

## Base and head

The same object and hook as hotcrm: `stage_entry_date` (date, `readonly`), `days_in_stage` (number, `readonly`), and a `beforeInsert` hook that stamps both when `stage_entry_date` is absent.

| case | base: hook saw `stage_entry_date` | base: stored | head: hook saw | head: stored |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| caller sends the readonly key (non-system) | `'2020-01-01'` | NULL / NULL | absent | `'2026-10-09'` / 0 |
| key absent (non-system) | absent | `'2026-10-09'` / 0 | absent | `'2026-10-09'` / 0 |
| system writer (`isSystem`) sends the key | `'2020-01-01'` | `'2020-01-01'` / NULL | `'2020-01-01'` | `'2020-01-01'` / NULL |
| a hook stamps the key unconditionally, and the caller sent it | `'2020-01-01'` | `'2026-10-09'` | absent | `'2026-10-09'` |

How each row was measured:

- **Rows 1 to 3, real engine over `driver-sql` (better-sqlite3):** base is `c8c803c293` with objectql built from that commit. Head is this branch.
- **Row 1, REST door:** `POST /api/v1/data/rro_opp` through `bootStack` with a sandboxed `body` hook. The base call answered 201 and stored NULL / NULL. The head call answered 201 and stored `'2026-10-09'` / 0.
  - The caller was the seeded admin, a non-system principal. The strip ran on the base call, which shows this: the forged value was not stored.
  - A freshly signed-up user had no create permission on the fixture object (403), so that user could not be used.
- **Row 4:** the engine over a recording driver, at head and with the hide ablated. The stored value is unchanged.
- **Batch:** the same on both paths. At base, row 0 of a batch (forged) stored NULL and row 1 stored the stamp. At head, both rows store the stamp.

## The change (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`)

- **Withhold, not strip, as on update.** Before the defaults and before `beforeInsert`, `withholdInsertReadonlyFromHooks` takes out every value that the post-hook static strip will take. It uses the same function (`stripReadonlyFields`), the same subject (`staticReadonlyInsertSubject`) and the same options (no `preserveAudit`), so the hide and the strip take the same caller keys. There is one named exception. Under `preserveAudit` the hide leaves the audit timeline visible, while the strip takes it unless the audit binder reinstates it. On a bare engine without `ObjectQLPlugin`, or for `created_by` / `updated_by` with no session user, such a value is shown to the hook and then stripped. The defaults then fill a withheld key the way they fill any absent key. So a forged `approval_status: 'approved'` is shown to the hook as its default `'draft'`, exactly what an honest caller's hook sees.
- **The strip does not move.** After the seal, `handBackWithheldInsertReadonly` puts the caller's values back wherever no hook wrote the key. The strip, its re-default, the WARN, `onFieldsDropped` and `strictReadonlyWrites` then judge the same payload as before.
  - A hook's own write is kept, and is never overwritten by a hand-back.
  - A `data.x = data.x` self-assignment of a withheld key follows the engine's rule:
    - with no `defaultValue` the hook reads `undefined`, the write is undone as on update, and the caller's value is stripped and reported. `undefined` is never stored.
    - with a `defaultValue` the hook re-assigns the default, which counts as the hook's write. The default is stored and nothing is reported.
- **Faults are explained.** The dispatch goes through `dispatchHooksExplainingWithheldReadonly`, the update path's wrapper. A hook that faults reaching through a withheld key gets a 400 that names the key.
  - `hook-withheld-readonly-fault.ts` gets a `beforeInsert` prescription, because a create has no `ctx.previous`.
  - The update message is byte-identical.

What update withholds (M2), measured on `origin/main`:

- **The set:** `stripReadonlyFields` over the full object schema. That covers static `readonly` and runtime-owned `autonumber`, but not `readonlyWhen`.
- **Exemptions:** `isSystem` (the whole pass) and the `preserveAudit` whitelist. A key the caller did not send (own property of the entry snapshot) is never a candidate, and `id` is excluded.
- **After the hooks:** seal, then hand back what the payload does not hold, undo a set-to-undefined, and narrow `hookWrittenKeys`. The caller's submission travels on `ctx.submitted`.

The insert set differs from that in three measured places:

- **Runtime-owned `autonumber` stays visible.** I first included it, and three existing pins went red. One is "the hook can still SEE the caller-submitted record number" (`engine-insert-runtime-owned-strip.test.ts`, #6339). The other two are the insert half of #14259's provenance seam (`engine-hook-provenance-sibling-seams.test.ts`). Moving that decision is not this card's, so the hide covers the static strip only.
- **The audit timeline stays visible under `preserveAudit`.** On a create the static strip takes `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at` and `updated_by` whatever the flag says. But the historical-import channel that the #15964 ruling kept working reinstates them through the audit binder's `preserveAudit` branch (`record.created_at ?? now`). Withholding them would erase every historical `created_at`. A business `readonly` column under `preserveAudit` is still withheld.
- **`sys_` and platform-internal (`managedBy`) objects keep their own guards.** The create strip's subject excludes them already, so nothing is withheld there.

There is no `ctx.submitted` on a create. The one in-repo `beforeInsert` reader that needs a caller's read-only value is the audit binder's `preserveAudit` branch, and it keeps seeing it.

Entry points (M3): `ObjectQL.insert` is the only `beforeInsert` dispatch site in the repo. Single insert, batch insert and `insertMany` all go through it. The engine has no upsert of its own. The protocol batch `upsert` create arm, REST `POST`, import and flows `create_record` all call `engine.insert`. Seeds write with `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT` (`isSystem: true`), so nothing is withheld for them.

## Docs touched

- `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`: TSDoc only. Two sentences said `beforeInsert` "is untouched" and "still receives the caller's own values". The `submitted` describe ("update only") stays true and is unchanged.
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`: rule 5 and the #16344 callout now cover insert.
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`: regenerated by `pnpm gen:system-context-census`, 118 to 119 elevation read sites. The +1 is the hide pass's non-system gate.

## Tests and gates

Head is `aa115f1c60`. The suites ran at `975f4b6690`; the only commit since then is `aa115f1c60`, which regenerates the census page and changes no code.

- `engine-insert-readonly-hook-input.test.ts` (new, 13 cases):
  - the ordering probe with a writable-key control;
  - the hotcrm shape;
  - a default shown in place of a forgery;
  - controls for `autonumber`, the system writer, strip reporting and the strict refusal;
  - a self-assignment no-op;
  - batch and `insertMany`;
  - `preserveAudit`;
  - the explained fault;
  - an update control.
- `hook-withheld-readonly-fault.test.ts`: one `beforeInsert` case.
- **Reverse verification:** `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor `hookViewSource[i] = hidden.row;` replaced with `void hidden.row;`. Result: 9 failed and 4 passed of 13. The four that stayed green are the controls that do not depend on the hide. The restore was verified: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Acceptance notes

- **Insert and update still differ on `autonumber`.** `beforeUpdate` does not see a caller-supplied `autonumber`, and `beforeInsert` still does (#6339's pin). A hook that issues its own record number only when the key is absent stands down on a forged one, and the sequence fills it. Not measured through a public door, and nobody has picked this up.
- **Changeset level.** Settled by the contract-tier review: `@objectstack/objectql` `minor` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, a BREAKING note and an ADR-0087 disposition, as the update-side twin (#16344) was. See Patch round 1.

## Patch round 1

This round changes text only, after the contract-tier review graded the narrowing BREAKING (FAIL on the semver level only; the engine change passed).

- **The changeset** `.changeset/22306-insert-readonly-withheld-from-before-insert.md`:
  - is now `'@objectstack/objectql': minor` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. That is the launch-window spelling of a breaking change, and pre mode stays on (`.changeset/pre.json`, tag `next`).
  - carries a BREAKING paragraph. It names what a `beforeInsert` handler reads on `ctx.input.data` on a non-system create, and the withheld set: `staticReadonlyInsertSubject`'s, minus the `autonumber` and `preserveAudit` audit-timeline edges.
  - names two answers that change at the REST door. Under `strictReadonlyWrites`, a self-assigning hook's launder is now refused (201 to 400). A hook or body that dereferences through a withheld key answers 400 where it answered 201.
  - carries one ADR-0087 disposition marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, in the comment form the gate reads.
- **Two sentences corrected:** the self-assignment sentence now states the engine's rule for a withheld key with a `defaultValue`, and "the two cannot disagree" now names the `preserveAudit` shown-but-stripped edge. Both corrections are in the changeset and in this body.
- **The two docs lines the review named as owed:** `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx` extends the persist-image sentence to `beforeInsert`, and census row 21 in `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` names the second `isSystem` read.
- **`@objectstack/spec` is not added to the changeset.** Its diff is TSDoc that documents objectql's behaviour. Listing it would print objectql's BREAKING note into spec's CHANGELOG under a `patch`, and an upgrader greps objectql's entry.
- **Gates:**
  - `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` reads the changeset as `BREAKING+clause-②-narrowing` with a `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition.
  - `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main` exits 0, and its level axis, run against this body as the PR event, is reported in the os-dev report.
  - `dispatch-gates --commands` was re-derived on the final commit, run and reconciled with `--ran`. The figures are in the os-dev report on the card.
- No code or test changed in this round.

## Merge round

This round merges `origin/main` `ca135dcc40` into the branch (merge commit `2008591e47`) and regenerates one page in `76bd4fd399`. Head is `76bd4fd399`.

- **Census skew.** `main`'s `ca135dcc40` and this branch each took `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` from 118 to 119, for different read sites.
  - The merge driver deferred the page (os-regen), so the merged page read 119 while the merged tree holds 120 sites. `check:system-context-census` was red on the merge commit with 6 declared-count mismatches (119 vs 120).
  - `pnpm gen:system-context-census` rewrote the counts, never by hand: 119 to 120 sites, 125 to 126 property reads, 116 to 117 behaviour-bearing.
  - The gate now exits 0 at 120 sites. Both sides' rows survive: against `main`, the page differs only by the counts and this branch's row-21 clause.
- **Readings at `76bd4fd399`:**
  - `@objectstack/objectql` `--project local`: 390 files, 7676 passed;
  - `--project repo`: 1 file, 5 passed;
  - `typecheck` (tsc plus `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0;
  - the pin files `engine-insert-readonly-hook-input.test.ts` and `hook-withheld-readonly-fault.test.ts`: 2 files, 24 passed.
  - `dispatch-gates --commands` derived the same 113 commands. All 113 ran and exited 0, and `--ran` reconciles them as 113 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
